title: Webhook verification
description: Framework-neutral TypeScript verification of inbound webhook HMAC-SHA256 signatures over raw body bytes with Web Crypto: generic hex, GitHub, Stripe, and Standard Webhooks/Svix, with secret rotation, timestamp tolerance, and a size-capped raw body reader.

notes: Uses only Web Crypto (crypto.subtle HMAC), Fetch Request/Headers, ReadableStream, TextEncoder, and atob; intended for Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers, and Hono. Only Node.js 22 was exercised by repository tests.
Requires access to the exact raw request body. Frameworks that parse JSON before the handler (for example Express json() or a body-parsing middleware) must be configured to expose raw bytes.
No runtime packages, environment reads, secret discovery, or network access occur at install, import, or call time.

configuration: Supply each signing secret from trusted server configuration; pass an array (1-10, current first) during rotation. String secrets are UTF-8 key bytes except Standard Webhooks, which expects whsec_<base64> (16-128 decoded bytes).
Stripe and Standard Webhooks accept toleranceSeconds (default 300, 1-86400, enforced in both directions) and an injectable clock returning epoch milliseconds.
readRawBody(request, maxBytes) requires an explicit cap from 1 byte to 64 MiB; choose the provider's documented maximum payload size.
Invalid configuration (missing/oversized secrets, bad tolerance, bad cap) throws a TypeError with a fixed message that never contains secret material; request input never throws.
limitations: Signature verification proves only that a holder of the secret produced the bytes. Replay protection beyond the timestamp window (deduplicating event or delivery IDs) and idempotent event processing belong to the application.
GitHub signatures carry no timestamp, so GitHub verification cannot reject old replays; deduplicate on X-GitHub-Delivery.
Asymmetric schemes (Standard Webhooks v1a/ed25519), SHA-1 X-Hub-Signature, Stripe v0, Slack, Shopify, Twilio, and other provider formats are not implemented.
timingSafeEqual is constant-time for equal-length byte arrays in JavaScript to the extent the engine allows; it returns early on differing lengths, which are public.
Tests ran on Node.js 22 with signatures computed independently by node:crypto; no live provider deliveries were received and other runtimes were not exercised.
